run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: The memory problem in namespace app-95 is an OOM kill of the orca application container, not a node-level or cluster-level memory event. Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h (owned by ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, owned by Deployment orca) ran once from 2026-11-21T07:19:23Z, reached an application-reported 109.4 MB of retained image data by 07:19:49Z, and its container was terminated with OOMKilled / exit code 137 at 2026-11-21T07:19:53Z; it restarted at 07:19:54Z and the new instance is repeating the same growth (62.7 MB by 07:20:00Z). The application's own startup logs state it is configured to 'Store all processed images for audit trail' and to cache thumbnails, and its logs show the retained set growing by 10 images / ~12 MB every 5 seconds against a 128Mi container memory limit. That fits unbounded in-process retention exhausting the container limit. The retention logic itself lives in the application code mounted from a Secret volume (app-code) that cannot be read in this Run, so the exact setting could not be verified, and Prometheus was unavailable throughout, so no cgroup memory series or OOMKilled state metric could be checked. No fault-injection flag for orca exists in the flagd ConfigMap, and no Evicted event or rollout was observed.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h in namespace app-95 has restartCount 1 and its container 'orca' lastState is terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137, startedAt 2026-11-21T07:19:23Z, finishedAt 2026-11-21T07:19:53Z; the container is now running, started 2026-11-21T07:19:54Z.

Deployment orca in namespace app-95 runs 1 replica (1 ready/available) with container 'orca' image python:3.9-slim, command ['python','/app/app.py'], resources limits memory 128Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 64Mi.

The application code is mounted into the container at /app from a Secret-backed volume named app-code (the secret name is redacted in the returned object), and the container environment declares only PYTHONUNBUFFERED and SERVICE_NAME.
orca startup logs of the post-restart instance state 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval'.

In the pre-kill instance, orca logs show monotonic growth of retained state: 20 images / 24.9 MB at 07:19:25Z, 50 images / 61.2 MB at 07:19:29Z, 70 images / 84.9 MB at 07:19:39Z, 90 images / 109.4 MB at 07:19:49Z, with the last line 'Processing image 99' at 07:19:53.858Z immediately before the 07:19:53Z OOMKill.

The restarted instance repeats the same pattern: 10 images / 13.5 MB at 07:19:56Z rising to 50 images / 62.7 MB by 07:20:00Z, i.e. the retained amount keeps growing after restart rather than staying flat.

Deployment orca carries annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1 and has a single ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f (owner Deployment orca, replicas 1), so no second ReplicaSet or template rollout is visible.

The events view across all namespaces inside the window returned exactly 6 events, all Normal and all in app-95: Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started on pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h, SuccessfulCreate on ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, and ScalingReplicaSet on Deployment orca ('Scaled up replica set orca-57fdcbf45f from 0 to 1') at 2026-11-21T07:19:23Z; no Evicted or node-related event was returned.
The only ConfigMap returned in namespace app-95 is kube-root-ca.crt; no application ConfigMap exists there to hold orca settings.

The OOMKill is caused by unbounded in-process retention inside orca: the 'store all processed images for audit trail' list plus the thumbnail cache keep every processed image, growing ~1.3-1.5 MB per image, so the container exceeds its 128Mi limit after roughly 90-100 images (109.4 MB of stored image data plus Python interpreter overhead).

The 128Mi memory limit is too small for the enabled retention behaviour, so even a bounded but nonzero audit cache would eventually OOM; this cannot be separated from the leak hypothesis without reading the code, which is mounted from the unreadable Secret app-code.

The problem will recur: the restarted container reproduced the same growth curve (13.5 MB to 62.7 MB within ~5 seconds of starting) and will reach the 128Mi ceiling again unless retention is bounded or the limit raised; only the portion up to 07:20:00Z was observed.

No Python-level memory failure text was observed: a filtered log query for error|memory|Memory|Killed|Traceback|Exception|OOM on pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h returned only the periodic 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' and 'Approximate memory used by stored images' lines, and the pre-kill instance simply stops at 'Processing image 99', which fits an external cgroup OOM kill rather than a handled in-process allocation error.

Fault-flag injection through the otel-demo flagd-config ConfigMap is not supported: that ConfigMap enumerates 11 flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad), all with defaultVariant 'off', and none references orca or a memory fault.

Pod eviction or node memory pressure is not supported: the container's own last termination reason is OOMKilled (not Evicted), and the events view returned no Evicted or node-related events, only Normal scheduling and startup events for the orca pod.

Bound the retention that the logs describe: cap or TTL-evict the processed_images list and the thumbnail cache (for example an LRU/maxlen collection or on-disk audit sink) instead of storing every processed image in memory, then re-measure working set against the 128Mi limit.

Read the application code mounted from Secret app-code (and any retention/audit toggle in it) with owner access, and profile the process (tracemalloc or py-spy per the approved runbook, which could not be executed here because the code is in an unreadable Secret and no exec tool exists in this Run) to confirm where the memory is retained.

Restore Prometheus/cAdvisor availability and alert on pod orca using container_memory_working_set_bytes against the 128Mi limit plus kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason='OOMKilled'} and container restart counts, since neither series could be read in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for every metrics query in this Run (get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so container_memory_working_set_bytes, kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason and restart-count series for pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h / Deployment orca were never read; cgroup-level memory growth and the metric label coverage are unknown, not zero.

The application code and any retention/audit configuration live in the Secret-backed volume app-code, which cannot be read; the exact setting that enables 'Storing all processed images for audit trail' and the thumbnail cache, and whether a toggle exists, could not be verified.
No orca traces are available: orca is not among the Jaeger services offered, so trace-level error or latency evidence for this service was not obtainable.
LimitRange objects could not be queried (kind not in the allowed list), so it is unknown whether the 128Mi/64Mi values come from a namespace default rather than the Deployment spec.

There is no change_history integration in this Run, so when Deployment orca was created or scaled from 0 to 1 and whether its pod template changed earlier cannot be established from the current objects.

Pod logs were bounded by the window: 42 lines at the end of the log view (after 07:20:01Z) and 153 lines in the filtered view were dropped as outside the query window, and only the newest ~200 lines were shown, so later growth or a subsequent OOM after 07:20:01Z is unknown.

A cluster-wide ConfigMap name search for orca returned no data (status no_data), which shows only that this query matched nothing; ConfigMaps without 'orca' in the name could still reference the workload and were not fully enumerated.
next_steps: Obtain owner access to the app-code Secret and inspect /app/app.py for the processed_images list and thumbnail cache retention logic and for any audit/retention environment toggle.
After bounding retention or raising the limit, re-check container memory working set and restart counts for pod orca-57fdcbf45f-ghr2h to confirm the growth curve flattens below the limit.
Add an OOMKilled/restart alert for Deployment orca in app-95 and verify that cAdvisor-based container_memory_working_set_bytes is being scraped for namespace app-95.
If unbounded storage is a product requirement, move the audit trail out of process memory (disk or object storage) instead of holding every image in RAM.

  webhook:
    cacheTTL: 0s
    enabled: true
  x509:
    clientCAFile: /etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt

  [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] Webhook
  webhook:
    cacheAuthorizedTTL: 0s
    cacheUnauthorizedTTL: 0s
cgroupDriver: systemd
cgroupRoot: /kubelet
clusterDNS:
- 10.96.0.10
clusterDomain: cluster.local
containerRuntimeEndpoint: ""
cpuManagerReconcilePeriod: 0s
crashLoopBackOff: {}
evictionHard:
  imagefs.available: 0%
  nodefs.available: 0%
  nodefs.inodesFree: 0%
evictionPressureTransitionPeriod: 0s
failSwapOn: false
fileCheckFrequency: 0s
healthzBindAddress: 127.0.0.1
healthzPort: 10248
httpCheckFrequency: 0s
imageGCHighThresholdPercent: 100
imageMaximumGCAge: 0s
imageMinimumGCAge: 0s
kind: KubeletConfiguration
logging:
  flushFrequency: 0
  options:
    json:
      infoBufferSize: "0"
    text:
      infoBufferSize: "0"
  verbosity: 0
memorySwap: {}
nodeStatusReportFrequency: 0s
nodeStatusUpdateFrequency: 0s
rotateCertificates: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
runtimeRequestTimeout: 0s
shutdownGracePeriod: 0s
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 0s
staticPodPath: /etc/kubernetes/manifests
streamingConnectionIdleTimeout: 0s
syncFrequency: 0s
volumeStatsAggPeriod: 0s

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] ${env:PROMETHEUS_COLLECTOR_PASSWORD}
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
